name: Superradiance: black-hole spins as boson detectors
summary: A rotating black hole amplifies waves with ω < mΩ_H, which is the wave version of the Penrose process. An ultralight boson whose Compton wavelength matches the horizon builds a superradiant cloud that spins the hole down and emits nearly monochromatic gravitational waves. Measured black-hole spins and searches for continuous waves therefore bound the masses of axion-like particles.

name: EMRIs map the Kerr multipole structure
summary: A compact object spiralling into a massive black hole completes ~10⁵ orbits in LISA's band. By Ryan's theorem, its phase evolution encodes all the mass and current multipoles of the central spacetime. Checking that they obey Kerr's relation tests the no-hair theorem more precisely than any electromagnetic probe can.
breaks: Extracting the multipoles needs second-order self-force waveforms and handling of environmental effects such as accretion disks. Both are still under development.
sources: Amaro-Seoane et al. (2017). "Laser Interferometer Space Antenna". [arXiv:1702.00786](https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.00786)

name: Linearized Einstein equations give gravitational waves
summary: Writing g = η + h and choosing harmonic (Lorenz) gauge turns the Einstein equations into a sourced wave equation. In transverse-traceless gauge two polarizations travel at c. Far from a slow source the leading retarded solution is the quadrupole formula, and its Isaacson energy flux drives binary inspirals.
map: \Box\bar h_{\mu\nu}=-\frac{16\pi G}{c^4}T_{\mu\nu},\ \ h^{TT}_{ij}=\frac{2G}{c^4r}\ddot I^{TT}_{ij},\ \ P=\frac{G}{5c^5}\langle\dddot Q_{ij}\dddot Q_{ij}\rangle

name: Linearized Einstein equations from entanglement first law
summary: In AdS/CFT the first law of entanglement for ball-shaped boundary regions, δS_A = δ⟨H_A⟩, is mapped through the Ryu–Takayanagi formula onto a bulk condition. That condition is equivalent to the bulk metric perturbation obeying the linearized Einstein equations. Holographic renormalization likewise identifies the Fefferman–Graham coefficients of a bulk solution with the boundary stress tensor.
breaks: The result is shown at linear order around pure AdS. Nonlinear Einstein dynamics and bulk regions far from the boundary need further assumptions.
sources: Ryu & Takayanagi (2006). "Holographic Derivation of Entanglement Entropy from AdS/CFT". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 96, 181602. [arXiv:hep-th/0603001](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/0603001)

name: Einstein equation as an equation of state
summary: Jacobson (1995) derived the Einstein equations by requiring the Clausius relation δQ = T dS on every local Rindler horizon, using the Unruh temperature and an entropy proportional to area. This result underpins emergent and entropic-gravity proposals in which the field equations are thermodynamic rather than fundamental.
breaks: The derivation assumes local equilibrium and an area law. With higher-curvature entropy or out-of-equilibrium horizons it needs extra terms, and whether gravity is truly emergent remains contested.

name: Semiclassical Einstein equation and backreaction
summary: QFT in curved spacetime feeds back into geometry through the semiclassical Einstein equation, whose source is the renormalized expectation value of the stress tensor. Renormalizing ⟨T⟩ produces the conformal trace anomaly. That anomaly drives the backreaction of evaporating black holes and anomaly-driven cosmologies.
breaks: The equation fails when stress-tensor fluctuations are comparable to the mean, for example in macroscopic superpositions of mass, where stochastic gravity or full quantum gravity is needed.

name: Einstein equations from worldsheet conformal invariance
summary: The closed string's massless spectrum contains a spin-2 graviton. Requiring the worldsheet sigma model on a curved background to stay conformally invariant (vanishing beta functions) imposes Einstein's equations coupled to the dilaton and B-field, plus α′ corrections. GR is therefore the low-energy limit of string theory.

name: Local Minkowski structure: SR as GR's tangent space
summary: By the equivalence principle, every freely falling frame is locally Minkowskian. GR replaces the global η_{μν} of special relativity by a curved g_{μν} whose tangent space at each point carries the Lorentz group, and SR laws hold to first order in Riemann normal coordinates. Curvature is exactly what no Lorentz transformation can remove.

name: Loop quantum cosmology: FLRW big bang becomes a bounce
summary: Quantizing the homogeneous FLRW sector with loop (holonomy) variables gives an effective Friedmann equation with a ρ² correction. The big-bang singularity of the classical FLRW solution is replaced by a bounce at a critical density of order the Planck density.
breaks: The bounce is derived in symmetry-reduced minisuperspace. Whether full LQG reproduces it, and how inhomogeneities behave, is not settled.

name: de Sitter and FLRW as arenas of particle creation
summary: The exact de Sitter and FLRW solutions are the standard backgrounds of QFT in curved spacetime. They host Parker's cosmological particle creation in an expanding FLRW universe, the Bunch–Davies vacuum, and the Gibbons–Hawking temperature of the de Sitter horizon, whose fluctuations seed inflationary perturbations.

name: Extra polarizations and dipole radiation beyond GR
summary: GR predicts two tensor polarizations and emission that starts at quadrupole order. Scalar–tensor theories add a breathing mode and dipole radiation from binaries with unequal sensitivities, entering at −1PN. Massive gravity adds dispersion and up to six polarizations. Waveform models capture these effects as deviations in the PN coefficients or as ppE terms.

name: GW170817 speed of gravity prunes Horndeski theories
summary: In Horndeski theories, couplings of the scalar to curvature (the G_{4,X}, G_{5,X} and G_{5,φ} terms) make tensor waves travel at a speed different from c on a cosmological background. GW170817 and GRB 170817A arrived 1.7 s apart after ~40 Mpc, bounding the gravity–light speed difference at the 10⁻¹⁵ level. This eliminated most such dark-energy models and also bounds Lorentz violation in the gravity sector.
breaks: The bound applies at LIGO frequencies (~100 Hz). Theories whose c_T deviates only at much lower frequencies, near the cutoff scale of the dark-energy effective theory, are not excluded by it.
sources: LIGO, Virgo, Fermi GBM & INTEGRAL (2017). "Gravitational Waves and Gamma-Rays from a Binary Neutron Star Merger: GW170817 and GRB 170817A". *Astrophys. J. Lett.* 848, L13. [arXiv:1710.05834](https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.05834)

name: Curvature-squared terms from quantum fields: R² gravity
summary: Renormalizing quantum matter fields on a curved background requires R² and R_{μν}R^{μν} counterterms in the gravitational action. Starobinsky's 1980 inflation model began as a quantum correction driven by the trace anomaly. Its R² term is now the prototype f(R) theory, which is equivalent to GR plus a scalar field (the scalaron).
map: f(R)=R+\frac{R^2}{6M^2}\ \Leftrightarrow\ \text{GR}+\text{scalaron of mass }M;\ \ \mathcal L_{\rm ct}\supset a_1R^2+a_2R_{\mu\nu}R^{\mu\nu}
sources: Sotiriou & Faraoni (2010). "f(R) theories of gravity". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 82, 451. [arXiv:0805.1726](https://arxiv.org/abs/0805.1726)

name: NR mergers calibrate inspiral–merger–ringdown waveforms
summary: Since Pretorius (2005), 3+1 simulations of binary black-hole and neutron-star mergers have supplied the strong-field merger stage that post-Newtonian theory cannot reach. Effective-one-body models, phenomenological models and NR surrogates are calibrated against NR catalogues and used as matched-filter templates. The simulations also fix the Kerr remnant whose ringdown ends the signal.
map: h^{\rm IMR}=h^{\rm PN/EOB}_{\rm insp}\oplus h^{\rm NR}_{\rm merger}\oplus\sum_{\ell mn}A_{\ell mn}e^{-i\omega_{\ell mn}t}
breaks: NR covers only the last tens of orbits and samples mass ratio, spin and eccentricity sparsely. Templates therefore interpolate, and they rely on PN/EOB for the early inspiral.
sources: Pretorius (2005). "Evolution of Binary Black-Hole Spacetimes". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 95, 121101. [arXiv:gr-qc/0507014](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/0507014)
Blanchet (2014; updated 2024). "Post-Newtonian Theory for Gravitational Waves". *Living Rev. Relativ.* [arXiv:1310.1528](https://arxiv.org/abs/1310.1528)

name: Numerical holography: Einstein equations in AdS
summary: Characteristic and 3+1 numerical-relativity methods were carried over to asymptotically AdS spacetimes to model far-from-equilibrium, strongly coupled plasmas. In the dual picture, horizon formation in the bulk is thermalization on the boundary. Colliding shock-wave simulations (Chesler–Yaffe) give hydrodynamization times relevant to heavy-ion collisions.
map: \text{bulk horizon formation}\leftrightarrow\text{boundary thermalization};\ \ \langle T_{\mu\nu}\rangle_{\rm CFT}\propto g^{(d)}_{\mu\nu}\ (\text{Fefferman–Graham})
breaks: AdS has a timelike boundary that needs boundary conditions with no counterpart in asymptotically flat NR. The dual is N=4 SYM, not QCD.

name: Binary-pulsar orbital decay confirms quadrupole formula
summary: The orbital period of the binary pulsar PSR B1913+16 decays as the Peters–Mathews quadrupole energy loss predicts, to about 0.2%. This was the first, indirect evidence that gravitational waves carry energy. The double pulsar J0737−3039 now tests the same formula to about 10⁻⁴.
sources: Hulse & Taylor (1975). "Discovery of a pulsar in a binary system". *Astrophys. J.* 195, L51. [doi:10.1086/181708](https://doi.org/10.1086/181708)

name: Strong-field tests of GR with compact-binary signals
summary: The PPN approach of fitting parametrized deviations from GR carried over to gravitational-wave data. LVK analyses test GR through shifts in the post-Newtonian phase coefficients, inspiral–merger–ringdown consistency, ringdown spectroscopy, and a graviton-mass bound from dispersion (m_g ≲ 1.3×10⁻²³ eV/c²). These probe the dynamical strong-field regime that solar-system and pulsar tests cannot reach.
breaks: Unlike the PPN framework, there is no complete theory-agnostic parametrization of the strong field. Waveform systematics can mimic deviations.
sources: Will (2014). "The Confrontation between General Relativity and Experiment". *Living Rev. Relativ.* 17, 4. [arXiv:1403.7377](https://arxiv.org/abs/1403.7377)

LIGO Scientific and Virgo Collaborations (2016). "Observation of Gravitational Waves from a Binary Black Hole Merger". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 116, 061102. [arXiv:1602.03837](https://arxiv.org/abs/1602.03837)

name: Pulsar timing: from binary-pulsar tests to PTAs
summary: PTAs extract nanohertz residuals with the same timing models built to test GR with binary pulsars (Shapiro delay, periastron advance, orbital decay). The expected quadrupolar Hellings–Downs correlation is itself a test that the waves are spin-2 and transverse-traceless, because scalar or vector polarizations give different overlap functions.
sources: NANOGrav Collaboration (2023). "The NANOGrav 15 yr Data Set: Evidence for a Gravitational-wave Background". *Astrophys. J. Lett.* 951, L8. [arXiv:2306.16213](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.16213)

name: Local Lorentz invariance as a pillar of the EEP
summary: The Einstein equivalence principle combines the weak equivalence principle, local Lorentz invariance and local position invariance, and Schiff's conjecture ties the three together. Michelson–Morley-type and clock-comparison experiments therefore test the same principle as Eötvös and redshift experiments. They are analysed jointly in Will's THεμ/PPN framework and in the gravity sector of the Standard-Model Extension.
sources: Will (2014). "The Confrontation between General Relativity and Experiment". *Living Rev. Relativ.* 17, 4. [arXiv:1403.7377](https://arxiv.org/abs/1403.7377)

name: Primordial GWs from amplified vacuum fluctuations
summary: On an FLRW background, each tensor polarization of linearized gravity obeys the mode equation of a massless, minimally coupled scalar. Inflation therefore amplifies its vacuum fluctuations exactly as in cosmological particle creation. The result is a nearly scale-invariant stochastic background whose power is set by the Hubble rate during inflation (the tensor-to-scalar ratio r).
breaks: The background has not yet been detected (only bounds on r). Late-time astrophysical backgrounds come from classical sources, not vacuum amplification.

name: Planck-scale discreteness vs Lorentz-invariance bounds
summary: Discrete or emergent spacetimes generically predict Planck-suppressed modified photon dispersion. Arrival-time bounds from gamma-ray bursts push the linear-order scale past the Planck energy, which disfavours lattice-like discreteness. Causal sets avoid the bound because Poisson sprinkling is statistically Lorentz invariant, and deformed rather than broken symmetry is another way out.
breaks: Quadratic-order effects (∝E⁴/E_Pl²) remain far below current sensitivity. Not every approach predicts dispersion: asymptotic safety and CDT make no generic Lorentz-violating prediction.

name: Rindler horizons and the Unruh effect
summary: A uniformly accelerated observer follows an orbit of a Lorentz boost (hyperbolic motion) and sees a Rindler horizon. Restricted to the Rindler wedge, the Minkowski vacuum is thermal with respect to the boost generator (Bisognano–Wichmann), which gives the Unruh temperature. Near any non-extremal horizon the geometry is approximately Rindler, so this flat-spacetime effect is the core of Hawking radiation.
map: x^2-c^2t^2=\frac{c^4}{a^2};\ \rho_{\rm R}\propto e^{-2\pi K_{\rm boost}},\ k_BT_U=\frac{\hbar a}{2\pi c}\leftrightarrow k_BT_H=\frac{\hbar\kappa}{2\pi c}
breaks: The Unruh temperature for laboratory accelerations is tiny (~4×10⁻²¹ K per m s⁻²), so it has not been observed directly.

name: Primordial black holes as dark matter
summary: PBHs are a non-particle dark-matter candidate; Hawking evaporation removes those below about 5e14 g and gamma-ray and CMB limits constrain slightly heavier ones, while lensing and GW limits leave the asteroid-mass window open.
sources: Carr et al. (2021). "Constraints on primordial black holes". *Rep. Prog. Phys.* 84, 116902. [arXiv:2002.12778](https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.12778)

name: Black-hole superradiance probes ultralight bosons
summary: A boson whose Compton wavelength matches a Kerr black hole forms hydrogen-like bound states that grow by superradiance while omega < m Omega_H, spinning the hole down; measured BH spins and continuous GW searches exclude axion masses near 1e-13 to 1e-11 eV.
sources: Arvanitaki & Dubovsky (2011). "Exploring the String Axiverse with Precision Black Hole Physics". *Phys. Rev. D* 83, 044026. [arXiv:1004.3558](https://arxiv.org/abs/1004.3558)
Arvanitaki et al. (2010). "String Axiverse". *Phys. Rev. D* 81, 123530. [arXiv:0905.4720](https://arxiv.org/abs/0905.4720)

name: The cosmological constant problem
summary: Lorentz invariance forces vacuum energy to enter the Einstein equations as rho_vac g_munu, so QFT zero-point energy, the Higgs potential and the QCD condensate all contribute to Lambda; naive estimates exceed the observed (2.2 meV)^4 by 50-120 orders of magnitude.
map: \langle T_{\mu\nu}\rangle_{\rm vac}=-\rho_{\rm vac}g_{\mu\nu}\Rightarrow\Lambda_{\rm eff}=\Lambda+8\pi G\rho_{\rm vac}/c^4,\ \rho_{\rm obs}\approx(2.2\,\text{meV})^4
sources: Weinberg (1989). "The Cosmological Constant Problem". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 61, 1. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.61.1](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.61.1)

name: Gravity as a gauge theory of the Lorentz group
summary: Gauging local Lorentz (Poincare) invariance gives the spin connection as gauge potential and the Riemann tensor as its field strength, so GR in tetrad form shares the fibre-bundle structure of Yang-Mills.
breaks: Not stated by the analyst.
sources: Utiyama (1956). "Invariant theoretical interpretation of interaction". *Phys. Rev.* 101, 1597. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.101.1597](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.101.1597)
Kibble (1961). "Lorentz invariance and the gravitational field". *J. Math. Phys.* 2, 212. [doi:10.1063/1.1703702](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.1703702)

name: Higgs inflation is a scalar-tensor theory
summary: A large non-minimal coupling xi h^2 R makes the SM Higgs the inflaton; transforming to the Einstein frame flattens the potential into the same plateau as Starobinsky R+R^2 gravity, giving n_s near 0.965 and r near 0.003.
sources: Bezrukov & Shaposhnikov (2008). "The Standard Model Higgs boson as the inflaton". *Phys. Lett. B* 659, 703. [arXiv:0710.3755](https://arxiv.org/abs/0710.3755)

name: Sub-millimetre tests of the inverse-square law
summary: ADD extra dimensions turn Newtonian gravity into a steeper power law below the compactification radius, parametrized as a Yukawa correction; torsion-balance tests of Newton's law below 0.1 mm bound n=2 ADD radii to tens of micrometres.
sources: Kapner et al. (2007). "Tests of the Gravitational Inverse-Square Law below the Dark-Energy Length Scale". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 98, 021101. [arXiv:hep-ph/0611184](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0611184)

name: Worldline EFT (NRGR) for compact binaries
summary: Non-relativistic GR treats compact bodies as point particles on worldlines with finite-size operators (tidal Love numbers) and integrates out potential and radiation gravitons with Feynman diagrams and dimensional regularization, the EFT toolkit of QCD applied to post-Newtonian inspirals.
map: S=-m\int d\tau+c_E\int d\tau\,E_{\mu\nu}E^{\mu\nu}+\dots,\quad v^2\sim Gm/r\ \text{as expansion parameter}
sources: Goldberger & Rothstein (2006). "An effective field theory of gravity for extended objects". *Phys. Rev. D* 73, 104029. [arXiv:hep-th/0409156](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/0409156)

name: Amplitudes compute post-Minkowskian binary dynamics
summary: On-shell scattering amplitudes, unitarity cuts and the eikonal give the conservative two-body Hamiltonian order by order in G (post-Minkowskian), now at 3PM-5PM, feeding EOB waveform models for LIGO and LISA.
breaks: Amplitudes give scattering (unbound) orbits most naturally; bound-orbit observables need analytic continuation (B2B maps) and radiation-reaction subtleties remain.
sources: Bern et al. (2019). "Scattering Amplitudes and the Conservative Hamiltonian for Binary Systems at Third Post-Minkowskian Order". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 122, 201603. [arXiv:1901.04424](https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.04424)

name: Nanohertz GWs from axion domain walls
summary: Collapsing domain walls of QCD-coupled axions, cosmic strings and QCD-scale phase transitions all produce stochastic GW backgrounds peaking near nanohertz; PTA spectra are fitted against these alongside supermassive-binary models.
breaks: The supermassive-black-hole-binary interpretation remains adequate; cosmological fits are not preferred decisively.
sources: Kitajima et al. (2024). "Gravitational waves from domain wall collapse, and application to nanohertz signals with QCD-coupled axions". *Phys. Lett. B* 851, 138586. [arXiv:2306.17146](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.17146)
NANOGrav Collaboration (2023). "The NANOGrav 15 yr Data Set: Search for Signals from New Physics". *Astrophys. J. Lett.* 951, L11. [arXiv:2306.16219](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.16219)

name: Cosmic strings from GUT symmetry breaking
summary: U(1) factors broken in GUT chains leave cosmic strings (possibly metastable via monopole nucleation) whose loops radiate a broad GW background; PTA amplitudes bound the string tension G mu, constraining breaking scales.
sources: NANOGrav Collaboration (2023). "The NANOGrav 15 yr Data Set: Search for Signals from New Physics". *Astrophys. J. Lett.* 951, L11. [arXiv:2306.16219](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.16219)
Caprini & Figueroa (2018). "Cosmological backgrounds of gravitational waves". *Class. Quantum Grav.* 35, 163001. [arXiv:1801.04268](https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.04268)

name: LISA tests first-order electroweak transitions
summary: Electroweak baryogenesis needs a strongly first-order transition; bubble collisions, sound waves and turbulence in that transition produce a GW background peaking near millihertz, squarely in the LISA band.
sources: LISA Cosmology Working Group (2024). "Gravitational waves from first-order phase transitions in LISA: reconstruction pipeline and physics interpretation". *JCAP* 10, 020. [arXiv:2403.03723](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.03723)
Caprini & Figueroa (2018). "Cosmological backgrounds of gravitational waves". *Class. Quantum Grav.* 35, 163001. [arXiv:1801.04268](https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.04268)

name: Graviton as a spin-2 quantum field
summary: Perturbative quantum gravity is QFT applied to the metric: expand g=eta+kappa h, quantize the massless spin-2 field with gauge fixing and ghosts as in Yang-Mills; the coupling kappa^2=32 pi G has mass dimension -2, so the theory is non-renormalizable and needs a UV completion.
sources: Burgess (2004). "Quantum gravity in everyday life: General relativity as an effective field theory". *Living Rev. Relativ.* 7, 5. [arXiv:gr-qc/0311082](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/0311082)
Donoghue (1994). "General relativity as an effective field theory: The leading quantum corrections". *Phys. Rev. D* 50, 3874. [arXiv:gr-qc/9405057](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/9405057)

name: GR as an effective field theory
summary: Power counting in E/M_Pl makes GR a predictive EFT: the Einstein-Hilbert term is leading, R^2 terms are suppressed, and the long-distance quantum correction to the Newtonian potential is computable and cutoff-independent, exactly like chiral perturbation theory.
sources: Burgess (2004). "Quantum gravity in everyday life: General relativity as an effective field theory". *Living Rev. Relativ.* 7, 5. [arXiv:gr-qc/0311082](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/0311082)
Donoghue (1994). "General relativity as an effective field theory: The leading quantum corrections". *Phys. Rev. D* 50, 3874. [arXiv:gr-qc/9405057](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/9405057)

name: Double copy: gravity = (gauge theory)^2
summary: Tree and loop gravity amplitudes are obtained from Yang-Mills amplitudes by replacing colour factors with kinematic numerators that obey the same Jacobi identities (BCJ), generalizing the KLT relations of string theory; the classical double copy maps Coulomb to Schwarzschild.
map: \mathcal A^{\rm YM}=\sum_i\frac{c_in_i}{D_i}\ \to\ \mathcal M^{\rm grav}=\sum_i\frac{n_i\tilde n_i}{D_i},\quad c_i\to n_i,\ g\to\kappa/2
sources: Bern, Carrasco & Johansson (2010). "Perturbative Quantum Gravity as a Double Copy of Gauge Theory". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 105, 061602. [arXiv:1004.0476](https://arxiv.org/abs/1004.0476)

name: AdS/CFT: bulk gravity equals boundary CFT
summary: Type IIB string theory on AdS5xS5 is conjectured to be exactly N=4 SU(N) super-Yang-Mills; the GKP-Witten dictionary maps bulk fields of mass m to CFT operators of dimension Delta, and the bulk on-shell action to the CFT generating functional.
sources: Maldacena (1998). "The Large N Limit of Superconformal Field Theories and Supergravity". *Adv. Theor. Math. Phys.* 2, 231. [arXiv:hep-th/9711200](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9711200)
Witten (1998). "Anti de Sitter space and holography". *Adv. Theor. Math. Phys.* 2, 253. [arXiv:hep-th/9802150](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9802150)
Gubser, Klebanov & Polyakov (1998). "Gauge theory correlators from noncritical string theory". *Phys. Lett. B* 428, 105. [arXiv:hep-th/9802109](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9802109)

name: Wilson loops as minimal string worldsheets
summary: In AdS/CFT the expectation value of a Yang-Mills Wilson loop is the exponential of minus the regularized area of a string worldsheet ending on the loop, giving the strong-coupling quark-antiquark potential V proportional to -sqrt(lambda)/L.
sources: Maldacena (1998). "Wilson loops in large N field theories". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 80, 4859. [arXiv:hep-th/9803002](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9803002)

name: Holographic QCD and confinement
summary: Confinement maps to a bulk geometry that caps off: in Witten's model the confinement-deconfinement transition is the Hawking-Page transition, Wilson loops are minimal string worldsheets with area law, and AdS/QCD models fit Regge trajectories.
breaks: QCD is not conformal in the UV, has N=3 and no supersymmetry; holographic QCD lacks asymptotic freedom and has no known exact string dual.
sources: Witten (1998). "Anti-de Sitter space, thermal phase transition, and confinement in gauge theories". *Adv. Theor. Math. Phys.* 2, 505. [arXiv:hep-th/9803131](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9803131)
Maldacena (1998). "Wilson loops in large N field theories". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 80, 4859. [arXiv:hep-th/9803002](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9803002)

name: Spin networks are gauge-invariant Wilson-loop states
summary: Ashtekar variables make GR an SU(2) connection theory; LQG states are holonomies (Wilson lines) on graphs labelled by spins, the same gauge-invariant basis used in Hamiltonian (Kogut-Susskind) lattice gauge theory, but on graphs that are not embedded in a fixed metric.
sources: Rovelli & Smolin (1990). "Loop space representation of quantum general relativity". *Nucl. Phys. B* 331, 80. [doi:10.1016/0550-3213(90)90019-A](https://doi.org/10.1016/0550-3213(90)90019-A)

name: CDT: lattice Monte Carlo for spacetime
summary: Causal dynamical triangulations regularize the gravitational path integral on simplicial lattices, sample it by Monte Carlo after Wick rotation, and seek a continuum limit at a second-order transition, the lattice-QCD strategy applied to geometry; a 4D de Sitter-like phase emerges.
map: Z=\sum_T\frac{1}{C_T}e^{-S_{\rm Regge}[T]}\ \leftrightarrow\ Z=\int\mathcal DU\,e^{-S_W[U]};\ \text{continuum limit at a 2nd-order point}
sources: Loll (2020). "Quantum Gravity from Causal Dynamical Triangulations: A Review". *Class. Quantum Grav.* 37, 013002. [arXiv:1905.08669](https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.08669)

name: Asymptotic safety: a UV fixed point for gravity
summary: Wilsonian and functional RG methods from QFT show evidence that Newton's dimensionless coupling g=Gk^2 flows to a non-Gaussian UV fixed point, making gravity non-perturbatively renormalizable, the gravitational analogue of asymptotic freedom with a non-zero fixed point.
sources: Niedermaier & Reuter (2006). "The Asymptotic Safety Scenario in Quantum Gravity". *Living Rev. Relativ.* 9, 5. [doi:10.12942/lrr-2006-5](https://doi.org/10.12942/lrr-2006-5)

name: Asymptotic safety predicted the Higgs mass
summary: Requiring the SM plus gravity to be asymptotically safe forces the Higgs quartic near zero at the Planck scale, predicting m_h of about 126 GeV with a few-GeV uncertainty two years before the 125 GeV discovery.
breaks: The prediction depends on assumed signs of gravitational anomalous dimensions; it is the same boundary condition as near-criticality of the SM vacuum and is not unique to asymptotic safety.
sources: Shaposhnikov & Wetterich (2010). "Asymptotic safety of gravity and the Higgs boson mass". *Phys. Lett. B* 683, 196. [arXiv:0912.0208](https://arxiv.org/abs/0912.0208)

name: Trace and gravitational anomalies fix Hawking flux
summary: Regularization breaks classical conformal and diffeomorphism symmetry just as it breaks axial symmetry (ABJ): the trace anomaly sources <T_mu^mu> in curved space, and demanding cancellation of the near-horizon gravitational anomaly reproduces the Hawking flux.
sources: Robinson & Wilczek (2005). "Relationship between Hawking Radiation and Gravitational Anomalies". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 95, 011303. [arXiv:gr-qc/0502074](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/0502074)

name: Bogoliubov transformations and vacuum ambiguity
summary: Canonical field quantization carries over to curved spacetime, but without a global timelike Killing vector the mode split into positive and negative frequency is not unique; in- and out-vacua related by Bogoliubov coefficients give particle creation (cosmological, Hawking, Unruh).
sources: Parker (1969). "Quantized Fields and Particle Creation in Expanding Universes. I". *Phys. Rev.* 183, 1057. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.183.1057](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.183.1057)

name: Higgs vacuum metastability in curved spacetime
summary: With m_h=125 GeV and m_t=173 GeV the Higgs quartic runs negative near 1e10-1e11 GeV, so the electroweak vacuum is metastable; gravitational corrections to the bounce (Coleman-De Luccia) and Higgs fluctuations during inflation decide whether our vacuum survives.
sources: Coleman & De Luccia (1980). "Gravitational effects on and of vacuum decay". *Phys. Rev. D* 21, 3305. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.21.3305](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.21.3305)
Degrassi et al. (2012). "Higgs mass and vacuum stability in the Standard Model at NNLO". *JHEP* 08, 098. [arXiv:1205.6497](https://arxiv.org/abs/1205.6497)

name: String compactifications as BSM model building
summary: Calabi-Yau, orbifold and brane-world compactifications generate gauge groups, chiral matter, axions, moduli and hidden sectors; BSM phenomenology inherits candidates (axiverse, moduli, GUT-like groups) and constraints (swampland conjectures) from string vacua.
breaks: The landscape of vacua is so large that few sharp low-energy predictions follow; no compactification uniquely reproduces the SM.
sources: Arvanitaki et al. (2010). "String Axiverse". *Phys. Rev. D* 81, 123530. [arXiv:0905.4720](https://arxiv.org/abs/0905.4720)

name: Compactified dimensions and the hierarchy problem
summary: String theory needs six extra dimensions; large (ADD) or warped (Randall-Sundrum) extra dimensions lower the fundamental gravity scale to TeV, and the RS warp factor is a slice of AdS5, so hierarchy models and holography share one geometry.
map: M_{\rm Pl}^2\simeq M_*^{n+2}R^n\ (\text{ADD}),\qquad m_{\rm TeV}=e^{-kr_c\pi}M_{\rm Pl}\ (\text{RS, AdS}_5\ \text{slice})
sources: Arkani-Hamed, Dimopoulos & Dvali (1998). "The Hierarchy problem and new dimensions at a millimeter". *Phys. Lett. B* 429, 263. [arXiv:hep-ph/9803315](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/9803315)
Randall & Sundrum (1999). "A Large Mass Hierarchy from a Small Extra Dimension". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 83, 3370. [arXiv:hep-ph/9905221](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/9905221)

name: Superstrings require supersymmetry
summary: Removing the bosonic-string tachyon and including fermions requires worldsheet supersymmetry, which with GSO projection yields spacetime supersymmetry; superstring compactifications are the main UV source of SUSY and supergravity model building.
breaks: Low-scale (TeV) SUSY is not predicted by string theory; the SUSY-breaking scale is unconstrained and LHC has not seen superpartners.
sources: Green & Schwarz (1984). "Anomaly cancellations in supersymmetric D = 10 gauge theory and superstring theory". *Phys. Lett. B* 149, 117. [doi:10.1016/0370-2693(84)91565-X](https://doi.org/10.1016/0370-2693(84)91565-X)

name: Green-Schwarz anomaly cancellation
summary: The same consistency principle that fixes SM hypercharges (gauge anomaly cancellation) fixes superstring gauge groups: gauge and gravitational anomalies of 10D supergravity cancel only for SO(32) or E8xE8 via the Green-Schwarz counterterm.
sources: Green & Schwarz (1984). "Anomaly cancellations in supersymmetric D = 10 gauge theory and superstring theory". *Phys. Lett. B* 149, 117. [doi:10.1016/0370-2693(84)91565-X](https://doi.org/10.1016/0370-2693(84)91565-X)

name: D-brane open strings give Yang-Mills
summary: The massless modes of open strings ending on N coincident D-branes are a U(N) gauge field plus adjoint scalars; their low-energy action is (super) Yang-Mills, so gauge theories arise as brane worldvolume theories, the starting point of AdS/CFT and brane-world model building.
sources: Polchinski (1995). "Dirichlet Branes and Ramond-Ramond Charges". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 75, 4724. [arXiv:hep-th/9510017](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9510017)
Witten (1996). "Bound states of strings and p-branes". *Nucl. Phys. B* 460, 335. [arXiv:hep-th/9510135](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9510135)

name: String theory born from hadron Regge trajectories
summary: The Veneziano amplitude was invented to fit linearly rising Regge trajectories of mesons; reinterpreted as vibrating strings, it predicted a massless spin-2 state that became the graviton once QCD took over the strong interaction.
sources: Veneziano (1968). "Construction of a crossing-symmetric, Regge-behaved amplitude for linearly rising trajectories". *Nuovo Cimento A* 57, 190. [doi:10.1007/BF02824451](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02824451)

name: Large-N planar diagrams equal string genus expansion
summary: In 't Hooft's large-N limit Feynman diagrams of SU(N) gauge theory organize by the genus of the surface they tile, weighted N^(2-2g), the same topological expansion as closed-string perturbation theory with g_s ~ 1/N; this is the structural root of gauge/string duality.
sources: 't Hooft (1974). "A planar diagram theory for strong interactions". *Nucl. Phys. B* 72, 461. [doi:10.1016/0550-3213(74)90154-0](https://doi.org/10.1016/0550-3213(74)90154-0)

name: Particles as unitary irreps of the Poincare group
summary: Wigner's classification defines an elementary particle as an irreducible unitary representation of the Poincare group, labelled by mass and spin (or helicity for m=0); spinor-helicity and little-group scaling in modern amplitudes are the same construction.
map: P^\mu P_\mu=-m^2c^2,\ W^\mu W_\mu=m^2c^2\hbar^2s(s+1);\quad m=0:\ \text{little group }ISO(2)\Rightarrow h=\pm s
sources: Wigner (1939). "On Unitary Representations of the Inhomogeneous Lorentz Group". *Ann. Math.* 40, 149. [doi:10.2307/1968551](https://doi.org/10.2307/1968551)

name: Invariant mass and collider kinematics
summary: Collider physics runs on four-momentum invariants: resonance discovery by invariant-mass peaks, sqrt(s) of colliding beams versus fixed targets, rapidity and transverse momentum as boost-friendly variables, and partonic s-hat = x1 x2 s.

name: Muon storage rings test time dilation
summary: The muon g-2 storage ring runs at the magic gamma=29.3, where the Thomas-BMT spin precession decouples from electric focusing; the dilated muon lifetime there confirmed SR time dilation to about 1e-3.
sources: Bailey et al. (1977). "Measurements of relativistic time dilatation for positive and negative muons in a circular orbit". *Nature* 268, 301. [doi:10.1038/268301a0](https://doi.org/10.1038/268301a0)

name: Neutrino speed bounds and the OPERA error
summary: Neutrino time of flight from SN1987A and long-baseline beams bounds |v-c|/c; the 2011 OPERA superluminal claim was traced to a faulty fibre connection, and superluminal neutrinos would lose energy by e+e- pair emission.
sources: Cohen & Glashow (2011). "Pair Creation Constrains Superluminal Neutrino Propagation". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 107, 181803. [arXiv:1109.6562](https://arxiv.org/abs/1109.6562)

name: Standard-Model Extension as an EFT of Lorentz violation
summary: The SME adds every Lorentz-violating operator built from SM fields contracted with fixed background tensors (a_mu, b_mu, c_munu, ...), turning clock, cavity, meson and astrophysical tests into bounds on a common coefficient table.
sources: Colladay & Kostelecky (1998). "Lorentz-violating extension of the standard model". *Phys. Rev. D* 58, 116002. [arXiv:hep-ph/9809521](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/9809521)
Kostelecky & Russell (2011). "Data Tables for Lorentz and CPT Violation". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 83, 11. [arXiv:0801.0287](https://arxiv.org/abs/0801.0287)

name: CPT violation requires Lorentz violation
summary: In an interacting unitary QFT, CPT violation implies Lorentz violation, so neutral-kaon and B-meson CPT interferometry bound the CPT-odd SME coefficients a_mu with sidereal-time modulation.
sources: Greenberg (2002). "CPT Violation Implies Violation of Lorentz Invariance". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 89, 231602. [arXiv:hep-ph/0201258](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0201258)

name: Hawking-Page transition as deconfinement
summary: In AdS, thermal gas and large black holes exchange dominance at the Hawking-Page temperature; holographically this is the confinement-deconfinement transition of the boundary gauge theory, with free energy jumping from O(N^0) to O(N^2).
breaks: Holographic transition is first-order at large N; QCD with physical quarks is a crossover at mu_B=0.
sources: Hawking & Page (1983). "Thermodynamics of Black Holes in anti-De Sitter Space". *Commun. Math. Phys.* 87, 577. [doi:10.1007/BF01208266](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01208266)
Witten (1998). "Anti-de Sitter space, thermal phase transition, and confinement in gauge theories". *Adv. Theor. Math. Phys.* 2, 505. [arXiv:hep-th/9803131](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9803131)

name: Gravitational form factors and proton pressure
summary: Matrix elements of the QCD energy-momentum tensor, the source of gravity, define the proton's gravitational form factors A, B, D; Ji's sum rule gives quark angular momentum and the D-term gives the internal pressure, extracted from deeply virtual Compton scattering.
breaks: Direct graviton scattering is unmeasurable; extraction relies on GPD models and dispersion relations, so the pressure profile is model dependent.
sources: Burkert, Elouadrhiri & Girod (2018). "The pressure distribution inside the proton". *Nature* 557, 396. [doi:10.1038/s41586-018-0060-z](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-018-0060-z)

Polyakov & Schweitzer (2018). "Forces inside hadrons: pressure, surface tension, mechanical radius, and all that". *Int. J. Mod. Phys. A* 33, 1830025. [arXiv:1805.06596](https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.06596)

name: Israel-Stewart causal hydrodynamics
summary: First-order (Navier-Stokes) relativistic viscous hydrodynamics is acausal and unstable; Israel and Stewart's second-order theory, built for relativistic fluids in GR, relaxes the shear tensor over a time tau_pi and underlies modern heavy-ion hydrodynamics.
sources: Israel & Stewart (1979). "Transient relativistic thermodynamics and kinetic theory". *Ann. Phys.* 118, 341. [doi:10.1016/0003-4916(79)90130-1](https://doi.org/10.1016/0003-4916(79)90130-1)

name: TOV equation: GR hydrostatics of nuclear matter
summary: The Einstein equations for a static perfect-fluid sphere give the Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff equation; each nuclear EOS P(epsilon) maps to a unique mass-radius curve and maximum mass, so 2 M_sun pulsars rule out soft EOSs.
sources: Oppenheimer & Volkoff (1939). "On Massive Neutron Cores". *Phys. Rev.* 55, 374. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.55.374](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.55.374)
Tolman (1939). "Static Solutions of Einstein's Field Equations for Spheres of Fluid". *Phys. Rev.* 55, 364. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.55.364](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.55.364)

name: BBN constrains G and extra gravitational fields
summary: The neutron-proton freeze-out temperature depends on the expansion rate H proportional to sqrt(G rho); primordial helium and deuterium bound any change of G between BBN and today to roughly 10-20% and limit scalar-tensor and extra-radiation models.
sources: Copi, Davis & Krauss (2004). "A new nucleosynthesis constraint on the variation of G". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 92, 171301. [arXiv:astro-ph/0311334](https://arxiv.org/abs/astro-ph/0311334)

name: Mergers probe a hadron-quark phase transition
summary: Neutron-star merger remnants reach several times saturation density at T of tens of MeV, a region of the QCD phase diagram heavy-ion collisions cannot reach; a strong first-order transition shifts the post-merger GW frequency away from the hadronic f2-radius relation.
breaks: Post-merger signals at kHz are below current sensitivity; the signature requires third-generation detectors.
sources: Most et al. (2019). "Signatures of quark-hadron phase transitions in general-relativistic neutron-star mergers". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 122, 061101. [arXiv:1807.03684](https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.03684)

Bauswein et al. (2019). "Identifying a first-order phase transition in neutron star mergers through gravitational waves". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 122, 061102. [arXiv:1809.01116](https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.01116)

name: Merger simulations with nuclear EOS
summary: GR hydrodynamic simulations of binary neutron-star mergers with tabulated finite-temperature nuclear EOSs predict prompt-collapse thresholds, remnant lifetimes and the post-merger f2 frequency, which correlates with stellar radius.
map: f_2\approx\text{few kHz},\quad f_2\propto\sqrt{M/R^3};\quad M_{\rm thr}\approx k\,M_{\rm max}^{\rm TOV},\ k\sim1.3\text{--}1.7
sources: Shibata et al. (2017). "Modeling GW170817 based on numerical relativity and its implications". *Phys. Rev. D* 96, 123012. [arXiv:1710.07579](https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.07579)

name: Merger ejecta and electron fraction from NR
summary: Which nuclei a merger makes depends on the ejecta electron fraction Y_e, set by shock heating and neutrino irradiation in NR simulations with neutrino transport; dynamical ejecta (Y_e < 0.25) make the third r-process peak, disk winds lighter elements.
breaks: Nucleosynthesis yields are sensitive to neutrino transport approximations and to unmeasured masses of very neutron-rich nuclei.
sources: Shibata et al. (2017). "Modeling GW170817 based on numerical relativity and its implications". *Phys. Rev. D* 96, 123012. [arXiv:1710.07579](https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.07579)

name: Mossbauer gamma lines measured gravitational redshift
summary: Pound and Rebka resolved a fractional shift of 2.5e-15 over 22.5 m by using the recoil-free 14.4 keV nuclear gamma transition of Fe-57, whose natural linewidth made the nuclear transition a clock fine enough to see gravity.
sources: Pound & Rebka (1960). "Apparent Weight of Photons". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 4, 337. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.4.337](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.4.337)

name: Equivalence-principle tests weigh nuclear binding
summary: Eotvos-type and MICROSCOPE tests compare materials whose mass-energy differs in nuclear binding and Coulomb energy fractions; a violating dilaton couples to these 'charges', so nuclear structure (B/A, Z(Z-1)/A^{4/3}) sets what an EP test probes.
sources: Damour (2012). "Theoretical aspects of the equivalence principle". *Class. Quantum Grav.* 29, 184001. [arXiv:1202.6311](https://arxiv.org/abs/1202.6311)

name: Love numbers enter the 5PN waveform phase
summary: The quadrupole induced by the companion's tidal field, Q = -lambda E, adds a term scaling as Lambda (v/c)^10 to the inspiral phase; computing k_2 needs a perturbed TOV solution, so EOS physics enters waveform models directly.
sources: Flanagan & Hinderer (2008). "Constraining neutron star tidal Love numbers with gravitational wave detectors". *Phys. Rev. D* 77, 021502. [arXiv:0709.1915](https://arxiv.org/abs/0709.1915)
Hinderer (2008). "Tidal Love Numbers of Neutron Stars". *Astrophys. J.* 677, 1216. [arXiv:0711.2420](https://arxiv.org/abs/0711.2420)

name: Tidal deformability from GW170817
summary: Tidal deformation of inspiralling neutron stars shifts the GW phase; GW170817 bounded the combined tidal deformability and hence radii near 11-13 km, excluding the stiffest nuclear equations of state.
sources: LIGO Scientific and Virgo Collaborations (2018). "GW170817: Measurements of neutron star radii and equation of state". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 121, 161101. [arXiv:1805.11581](https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.11581)

name: GW170817 kilonova as an r-process site
summary: The GW-localized merger GW170817 produced a kilonova whose red, lanthanide-rich emission powered by r-process decay showed that neutron-star mergers make heavy elements, tying nuclear masses and beta rates to GW sources.
map: L(t)\propto M_{\rm ej}\,\dot\epsilon(t),\ \dot\epsilon\propto t^{-1.3};\quad M_{\rm ej}\sim0.05\,M_\odot
sources: Kasen et al. (2017). "Origin of the heavy elements in binary neutron-star mergers from a gravitational-wave event". *Nature* 551, 80. [arXiv:1710.05463](https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.05463)

name: BBN bound on primordial GW backgrounds
summary: Any primordial GW background present before BBN is extra radiation and raises N_eff; the light-element abundances cap its integrated energy density, a benchmark that LISA and PTA cosmological interpretations must respect.
sources: Caprini & Figueroa (2018). "Cosmological backgrounds of gravitational waves". *Class. Quantum Grav.* 35, 163001. [arXiv:1801.04268](https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.04268)

name: Holographic thermalization of heavy-ion collisions
summary: Colliding gravitational shock waves in AdS5 form a black brane within about 1/T, modelling rapid hydrodynamization of the fireball; horizon formation plays the role of thermalization.
breaks: Infinite-coupling, infinite-N model; real collisions have weak-coupling early stages (glasma) and finite N.
sources: Chesler & Yaffe (2011). "Holography and colliding gravitational shock waves in asymptotically AdS5 spacetime". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 106, 021601. [arXiv:1011.3562](https://arxiv.org/abs/1011.3562)

name: Fluid/gravity correspondence
summary: Slowly varying black branes in AdS5 are dual to solutions of relativistic viscous hydrodynamics; the bulk Einstein equations order by order in gradients yield the transport coefficients of second-order hydrodynamics used in heavy-ion codes.
sources: Bhattacharyya et al. (2008). "Nonlinear Fluid Dynamics from Gravity". *JHEP* 02, 045. [arXiv:0712.2456](https://arxiv.org/abs/0712.2456)

name: Trailing strings and holographic jet quenching
summary: A heavy quark crossing a strongly coupled plasma is a string trailing into a black-brane horizon; the drag force and jet quenching parameter q-hat follow in closed form, giving estimates comparable to RHIC/LHC energy-loss data.
breaks: N=4 SYM rather than QCD, and the perturbative early-time regime of jets is missing.
sources: Gubser (2006). "Drag force in AdS/CFT". *Phys. Rev. D* 74, 126005. [arXiv:hep-th/0605182](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/0605182)
Liu, Rajagopal & Wiedemann (2006). "Calculating the jet quenching parameter from AdS/CFT". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 97, 182301. [arXiv:hep-ph/0605178](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0605178)

name: eta/s = 1/4pi from black-brane horizons
summary: Shear viscosity of a strongly coupled plasma equals the absorption of gravitons by a black-brane horizon; for every two-derivative gravity dual eta/s = hbar/4pi k_B, close to the small eta/s extracted from RHIC/LHC flow.
breaks: N=4 SYM is conformal, supersymmetric and large-N; QCD near T_c is none of these, and the 1/4pi value is violated by higher-curvature corrections.
sources: Kovtun, Son & Starinets (2005). "Viscosity in strongly interacting quantum field theories from black hole physics". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 94, 111601. [arXiv:hep-th/0405231](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/0405231)

name: Hadronization as Unruh radiation
summary: Thermal hadron yields with a universal T near 160 MeV in e+e-, pp and AA have been modelled as Unruh radiation from quarks decelerated by the string tension at a confinement horizon, with T = a/2pi and a ~ sqrt(sigma).
breaks: The confinement 'horizon' is not a spacetime horizon; universal thermal yields also follow from statistical hadronization without any Unruh mechanism.
sources: Castorina, Kharzeev & Satz (2007). "Thermal hadronization and Hawking-Unruh radiation in QCD". *Eur. Phys. J. C* 52, 187. [arXiv:0704.1426](https://arxiv.org/abs/0704.1426)

name: Rapidity and Bjorken boost-invariant flow
summary: Lorentz boosts along the beam add rapidities, so a boost-invariant expansion depends only on proper time tau; Bjorken's solution of relativistic hydrodynamics gives the initial energy-density estimate used in every heavy-ion analysis.
sources: Bjorken (1983). "Highly relativistic nucleus-nucleus collisions: The central rapidity region". *Phys. Rev. D* 27, 140. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.27.140](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.27.140)

name: Q-values and the direct test of E=mc^2
summary: Nuclear reaction energetics are mass-energy equivalence in action: Q = (sum m_i - sum m_f)c^2; comparing neutron-capture gamma energies with Penning-trap mass differences verified E=mc^2 to 4e-7.
sources: Rainville et al. (2005). "A direct test of E=mc^2". *Nature* 438, 1096. [doi:10.1038/4381096a](https://doi.org/10.1038/4381096a)

name: Hughes-Drever tests with nuclear spins
summary: Nuclear magnetic resonance of nuclei with J > 1/2 (Li-7, and modern He-3/Xe-129 comagnetometers) searches for quadrupole splitting varying with sidereal orientation; shell-model wavefunctions convert the bounds into limits on proton and neutron SME coefficients near 1e-30 GeV.
breaks: Interpreting a bound requires a nuclear model of which nucleons carry the spin, adding model dependence.
sources: Hughes, Robinson & Beltran-Lopez (1960). "Upper Limit for the Anisotropy of Inertial Mass from Nuclear Resonance Experiments". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 4, 342. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.4.342](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.4.342)

name: Area laws: black-hole and entanglement entropy
summary: Entanglement entropy of a field across a surface scales with its area, as does Bekenstein-Hawking entropy; in gapped topological phases the area law has a universal constant correction -gamma = -ln D, the same diagnostic used for long-range entanglement.
breaks: The entanglement coefficient alpha is cutoff-dependent; matching 1/4G needs renormalization of Newton's constant, while gamma has no BH counterpart.
sources: Srednicki (1993). "Entropy and area". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 71, 666. [arXiv:hep-th/9303048](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9303048)
Kitaev & Preskill (2006). "Topological Entanglement Entropy". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 96, 110404. [arXiv:hep-th/0510092](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/0510092)

name: SYK: strange metal and near-extremal black hole
summary: The Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev model of randomly interacting fermions, rooted in a random-magnet spin fluid, has an extensive zero-temperature entropy and emergent reparametrization symmetry matching near-extremal charged black holes and JT gravity in AdS2; it also maximizes chaos.
sources: Sachdev (2015). "Bekenstein-Hawking Entropy and Strange Metals". *Phys. Rev. X* 5, 041025. [arXiv:1506.05111](https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.05111)
Maldacena & Stanford (2016). "Remarks on the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev model". *Phys. Rev. D* 94, 106002. [arXiv:1604.07818](https://arxiv.org/abs/1604.07818)

name: Type-II Weyl cones as analogue horizons
summary: A tilted Weyl cone is a Weyl fermion in an effective Painleve-Gullstrand metric whose shift vector is the tilt; where the tilt exceeds the Fermi velocity (type I to type II) the cone tips over like light cones at a horizon, and Hawking-like tunnelling has been proposed at such interfaces.
map: H=\hbar\mathbf t\cdot\mathbf k+\hbar v_F\boldsymbol\sigma\cdot\mathbf k\ \leftrightarrow\ ds^2=-c^2dt^2+(d\mathbf x-\mathbf v\,dt)^2,\ |\mathbf t|=v_F\ \text{at horizon}
breaks: No Einstein dynamics or backreaction; lattice cutoff, disorder and electron interactions are not small, and the emitted 'temperature' would be tiny.
sources: Volovik (2016). "Black hole and Hawking radiation by type-II Weyl fermions". *JETP Lett.* 104, 645. [arXiv:1610.00521](https://arxiv.org/abs/1610.00521)

name: Chaos bound and Planckian dissipation
summary: Black holes saturate the bound on the Lyapunov exponent of out-of-time-order correlators and are the fastest scramblers; strange metals show a transport rate near the same Planckian scale k_B T/hbar, suggesting a common bound on dissipation in matter without quasiparticles.
breaks: No theorem ties lambda_L to the momentum-relaxation rate that sets resistivity; the chaos bound is rigorous, the transport 'bound' is empirical and has counterexamples.
sources: Maldacena, Shenker & Stanford (2016). "A bound on chaos". *JHEP* 08, 106. [arXiv:1503.01409](https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.01409)
Sekino & Susskind (2008). "Fast Scramblers". *JHEP* 10, 065. [arXiv:0808.2096](https://arxiv.org/abs/0808.2096)

name: Dislocations as torsion, disclinations as curvature
summary: The continuum theory of crystal defects is Riemann-Cartan geometry: the Burgers vector is the closure failure (torsion) and the Frank angle the rotation holonomy (curvature); a disclination line has the conical metric of a cosmic string.
map: b^a=\oint e^a{}_\mu dx^\mu=\iint T^a\ (\text{torsion}),\quad \Omega=\iint R\ (\text{curvature});\ ds^2=dr^2+\alpha^2r^2d\phi^2+dz^2
breaks: Euclidean signature and elastic energy replace the Einstein-Hilbert action; the 'geometry' is a bookkeeping device with no propagating gravitons.

name: Hall viscosity and gravitational response
summary: Coupling a quantum Hall fluid to a background spatial metric and spin connection defines Hall viscosity eta_H = hbar s-bar n/2 and the Wen-Zee shift on curved surfaces; Luttinger's fictitious gravitational potential likewise defines thermal-Hall response.
map: \eta_H=\tfrac12\hbar\bar s\,n,\quad N_\phi=\nu^{-1}N-\mathcal S\ (\text{sphere}),\quad \mathcal L_{\rm WZ}\propto\frac{\nu\bar s}{2\pi}\omega\wedge dA
breaks: The background metric is a probe, not dynamical gravity, and the fluid is non-relativistic.
sources: Hoyos & Son (2012). "Hall Viscosity and Electromagnetic Response". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 108, 066805. [arXiv:1109.2651](https://arxiv.org/abs/1109.2651)
Luttinger (1964). "Theory of Thermal Transport Coefficients". *Phys. Rev.* 135, A1505. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.135.A1505](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.135.A1505)

name: Gravity Probe B gyroscopes read by SQUIDs
summary: Gravity Probe B measured geodetic and frame-dragging precession of niobium-coated quartz rotors through the London moment of the spinning superconductor, read out by SQUID magnetometers at milliarcsecond resolution.
sources: Everitt et al. (2011). "Gravity Probe B: Final Results of a Space Experiment to Test General Relativity". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 106, 221101. [arXiv:1105.3456](https://arxiv.org/abs/1105.3456)

name: Chiral 'graviton' modes of FQH liquids
summary: Haldane's geometric picture gives a fractional quantum Hall fluid a dynamical unimodular intrinsic metric; its long-wavelength fluctuation is a spin-2 chiral mode (GMP magnetoroton), whose chirality has been probed with circularly polarized Raman scattering, like a GW helicity-2 mode.
breaks: The mode is gapped, non-relativistic and lives on a lattice-free 2D fluid without diffeomorphism invariance; it is spin-2 only in the sense of its rotation quantum number.
sources: Haldane (2011). "Geometrical Description of the Fractional Quantum Hall Effect". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 107, 116801. [arXiv:1106.3375](https://arxiv.org/abs/1106.3375)

name: Amorphous mirror coatings limit LIGO thermal noise
summary: In the most sensitive LIGO band the floor is Brownian thermal noise of the amorphous Ta2O5/SiO2 mirror coatings, set via fluctuation-dissipation by their mechanical loss angle, which comes from two-level systems in the glass.
map: S_x(f)=\frac{2k_BT}{\pi^2f^2}\frac{W_{\rm diss}}{F_0^2},\quad W_{\rm diss}\propto\phi_{\rm coat}\ (\text{loss angle})
sources: Levin (1998). "Internal thermal noise in the LIGO test masses: A direct approach". *Phys. Rev. D* 57, 659. [arXiv:gr-qc/9707013](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/9707013)

name: Liquid crystals test cosmic-string network scaling
summary: Cosmic-string GW backgrounds rest on the Kibble mechanism and scaling of string networks; quenched nematic liquid crystals form and coarsen string networks that can be filmed, giving laboratory checks of defect formation and scaling.
breaks: Nematic strings move dissipatively, not relativistically (no Nambu-Goto dynamics), and do not radiate gravitational waves; loop production and GW spectra cannot be tested this way.
sources: Chuang, Durrer, Turok & Yurke (1991). "Cosmology in the Laboratory: Defect Dynamics in Liquid Crystals". *Science* 251, 1336. [doi:10.1126/science.251.4999.1336](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.251.4999.1336)

name: Cryogenic crystalline test masses
summary: KAGRA uses 20 K sapphire and Einstein Telescope/LIGO Voyager plan cryogenic silicon test masses, chosen for low phonon loss and for silicon's vanishing thermal expansion near 123 K, which kills thermoelastic noise.
sources: Punturo et al. (2010). "The Einstein Telescope: A third-generation gravitational wave observatory". *Class. Quantum Grav.* 27, 194002. [doi:10.1088/0264-9381/27/19/194002](https://doi.org/10.1088/0264-9381/27/19/194002)

name: Dirac-fluid hydrodynamics near the KSS bound
summary: Near charge neutrality graphene electrons form a nearly relativistic Dirac fluid with small eta/s and violated Wiedemann-Franz law; relativistic and holographic hydrodynamics developed for the QGP and black branes describe its transport.
breaks: Graphene is weakly coupled (alpha_g of order 1 but with log running), has disorder and phonons, and has no gravity dual.
sources: Crossno et al. (2016). "Observation of the Dirac fluid and the breakdown of the Wiedemann-Franz law in graphene". *Science* 351, 1058. [arXiv:1509.04713](https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.04713)

name: MERA tensor networks as discrete AdS
summary: The multiscale entanglement renormalization ansatz built for critical spin chains has a hyperbolic network geometry; minimal cuts through it reproduce Ryu-Takayanagi, so condensed-matter numerics became a toy model of emergent bulk space and holographic codes.
sources: Swingle (2012). "Entanglement Renormalization and Holography". *Phys. Rev. D* 86, 065007. [arXiv:0905.1317](https://arxiv.org/abs/0905.1317)

name: Holographic strange metals (AdS/CMT)
summary: Charged black branes model compressible quantum-critical matter without quasiparticles: horizon geometry sets T-linear resistivity, Planckian relaxation and non-Fermi-liquid spectral functions in bottom-up holographic models.
breaks: No known microscopic lattice Hamiltonian has a controlled gravity dual; large-N and strong coupling are assumptions, and bottom-up models fit rather than derive cuprate data.
sources: Hartnoll (2009). "Lectures on holographic methods for condensed matter physics". *Class. Quantum Grav.* 26, 224002. [arXiv:0903.3246](https://arxiv.org/abs/0903.3246)

name: Holographic superconductors: hairy black holes
summary: Below a critical temperature a charged black brane becomes unstable to growing charged scalar hair; the boundary dual is a condensate that breaks U(1), with an optical-conductivity gap and a gap-to-Tc ratio larger than BCS.
breaks: The boundary U(1) is global, not dynamical, so there is no Meissner effect without extra gauging; mean-field exponents follow from large N.
sources: Hartnoll, Herzog & Horowitz (2008). "Building a Holographic Superconductor". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 101, 031601. [arXiv:0803.3295](https://arxiv.org/abs/0803.3295)

name: Emergent gauge fields and gravity from many-body order
summary: String-net condensation in lattice spin models gives emergent photons and fermions, raising the question of whether gravity can emerge the same way; emergent-gravity programmes (Volovik, Wen) use topological order as a template.
breaks: Weinberg-Witten forbids a massless spin-2 particle from a Lorentz-covariant conserved stress tensor, and emergent Lorentz invariance is not exact on a lattice; no model yields Einstein gravity.
sources: Levin & Wen (2005). "String-net condensation: A physical mechanism for topological phases". *Phys. Rev. B* 71, 045110. [arXiv:cond-mat/0404617](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0404617)
Weinberg & Witten (1980). "Limits on massless particles". *Phys. Lett. B* 96, 59. [doi:10.1016/0370-2693(80)90212-9](https://doi.org/10.1016/0370-2693(80)90212-9)

name: Strained graphene: Dirac fields in curved space
summary: Low-energy graphene electrons obey a 2+1D Dirac equation; strain and ripples enter as pseudo-gauge fields and a position-dependent tetrad, so curved-space Dirac methods describe pseudo-Landau levels in nanobubbles and suggest Hawking/Unruh analogues.
breaks: v_F is 1e6 m/s, not c; Coulomb interactions are instantaneous, valleys carry opposite pseudo-fields, and the 'metric' is not dynamical.
sources: Vozmediano, Katsnelson & Guinea (2010). "Gauge fields in graphene". *Phys. Rep.* 496, 109. [arXiv:1003.5179](https://arxiv.org/abs/1003.5179)

name: Mixed axial-gravitational anomaly in Weyl semimetals
summary: The chiral anomaly of Weyl fermions has a gravitational piece proportional to the curvature, which via Luttinger's temperature-as-gravitational-potential maps to a thermal-gradient term; positive magneto-thermoelectric conductance in NbP was reported as its signature.
breaks: Thermal-transport signals have competing phonon and conventional explanations; the anomaly attribution is contested.
sources: Gooth et al. (2017). "Experimental signatures of the mixed axial-gravitational anomaly in the Weyl semimetal NbP". *Nature* 547, 324. [arXiv:1703.10682](https://arxiv.org/abs/1703.10682)

name: Emergent Lorentz boosts with c -> v_F in graphene
summary: Graphene's massless Dirac Hamiltonian is invariant under boosts with v_F replacing c; boosting away an in-plane E field predicts the collapse of Landau levels when E/B reaches v_F, as in E x B drift with E > cB.
breaks: Emergent symmetry only at low energy: trigonal warping, lattice and instantaneous Coulomb interaction break it.
sources: Lukose, Shankar & Baskaran (2007). "Novel Electric Field Effects on Landau Levels in Graphene". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 98, 116802. [arXiv:cond-mat/0611406](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0611406)
